beta_new: From the high pass south of the Birdwood Lakes, turn onto the northwest ridge and follow it up. The lower half is a loose, exposed scramble that most parties find stays near Class 3. Higher up the ridge steepens and narrows, with a short knife-edge and a few harder moves in the 5.4-5.5 range; rock quality is poor, so test every hold.

moves.from: Many parties carry a rope, a small rack and slings for the harder steps.

value.text: A rope, a small rack and slings for the harder steps.

beta_new: Above the tarns, cross a faint headwall right to left, follow the glacial stream to a shallow col, and cross the snowy plateau to the ridge. The crux is two narrow notches in the ridge, each downclimbed and then climbed out of the far side at about 5.4. Fixed anchors and large boulders allow a rappel station if you want to protect them. Past the notches, a plain hike leads to the top.

Begin up and to the right of the neighbouring Blow Fly line and follow the thin crack past an old piton to reach a bolt on the face. From there the face continues leftward and a little higher, with a runout, until you meet the fourth bolt of that neighbour and finish up it.

Begin just to the right of the neighbouring route on the left and climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a flake, then step left into the prominent crack. Follow it beside a small roof, trending back right above the roof to a fixed piton in a second crack, and finish up the face to the top.

The first pitch is shared with Doug's Dandy. On the second pitch, shift a bit south and pull the overhang, then scramble rightward and higher to a slim ledge heading south. On the third, traverse past a bolt and choose among a handful of variations to the summit area, then scramble east to the top of the Head.

Share the start with Two Cams & Jam and follow the wide, right-curving crack until it flattens out horizontally. At that point leave it and climb directly up the face, going over the zenolith, to the top.
Begin next to Bubblenutz on its right and move rightward over a small roof onto a smooth slab and into a corner and up the face above.

moves.from: For the short corner, bring a few stoppers plus cams to roughly 2 inches.

beta_new: Begin below and to the left of Gravity and climb the obvious dark streak to bolts on the right. Continue up the face past those bolts to a thin crack, then follow the crack to the top.

Begin around the corner up and to the right of Young Monkeys, and follow the horizontal crack leftward until you are just right of the prow. Then climb the face rightward, clipping three bolts, to the fourth, continue right to the fifth, then drift left toward bolt six, and finish by heading rightward and above the seventh bolt to the top.

Start on the right-facing flake just left of the left-facing dihedral and climb it to a horizontal crack, watching for an owl that may be nesting. Then step right into a thin crack and follow it to the top, where the hardest moves are.

The first pitch begins by scrambling to the foot of a short dihedral, which you climb to a sequence of roofs. Work through the roofs to a stemming section, then layback to the belay. Loose rock is likely, and gear can be fiddly to place.

Work up and leftward over easy ground to a flake and climb the right side of it until you can move out left and higher to the two-bolt belay, the same belay that tops the first pitch of Hanging Gardens. Climb the face above for a full rope length with one bolt along the way to reach the top.
Start on the south side of the pinnacle and climb that side directly to the summit, clipping the single bolt on the way.

Start at the right end of the wall and climb the face, clipping a single bolt, then follow a seam by two horizontal cracks and a boulder that is perched there. This brings you under a hand crack, and a short face section above gets you to the top.
Plan on bringing two long ropes, about 165 feet each, to rappel back down to the ledge after finishing.
Step right from the small boulder onto the face and climb past a pair of bolts and a horizontal crack to a two-bolt belay. Expect a bit of a runout, on easy terrain, near the top.

The first pitch follows the obvious crack on aid, clipping aid bolts to a small ledge above an overhang. The second continues up the crack with free and aid moves, clipping four bolts, to a sling belay. Then traverse right on a ledge past a bolt to a stance, and finish up a ramp angling rightward to the summit. A variation exits left from the sling belay.

Share the start with North Central Variation. The first pitch traverses right to a hanging belay on two bolts, and the second goes straight up for around sixty feet, clipping three bolts, to a good ledge. The third pitch continues rightward.
Find the line a short way right of Wormsign and ascend a run of broken flakes that face left to reach the bolted slab above.
The route starts on the face and then moves to an arete. Near the top it is awkward to stay on the arete, since easier-looking terrain lies leftward, yet the bolts are on the arete itself.

Start low and to the right of Loafer's Choice and climb the face to a bolt beneath a roof. Get over the roof, then climb the face using the leftmost crack until you can step out left onto the arete and follow it to the top.

Step off the flake onto the face to enter the vertical crack and follow it past a bolt, where unusual pocket moves lead to a last bulge. Get over the bulge via the crack, then continue up the face past two bolts, trending left to the top.
Pick the left-hand flake, the one with the whitewashed tip, and climb the south face of the flake past its bolts to the top.

moves.from: To get off, scramble down and to the right.

beta_new: Start a short way right of Black Streak and layback the flake up to a ledge, which holds the hardest moves. Continue up the right-facing corner, clipping one bolt, then finish in a thin crack to the top.

Start at a granite outcrop around the middle of the east wall and scramble to a large ledge beneath an overhang. Next, shift south a few feet and pull the overhang, then scramble to a belay bolt. After walking north to a big saguaro, traverse north past bolts and an overhang to a buttress, climb it to a belay, and take gullies east to the summit.

Look for the small amphitheater in the middle of the rock, with a decayed arch at left and a gentle off-width on the right. Work a bit up the arch, then go leftward by a bolt to a horizontal break and go on up beyond several additional bolts to a hanging belay on two bolts. On the second pitch, get out under the overhang to either side.

Begin in the shallow corner twenty feet right of East Face. The second pitch heads up and rightward into an overhanging corner, and the third returns rightward to an amber-colored wall and a horizontal break that ends at a belay with two bolts.

On the final pitch step left, climb flakes past an old bolt ladder, traverse leftward to the overhangs, and pass them with a swing and a touch of aid.

Begin up a chute that takes little gear, and past a bulge move left to an arch that faces left. Where the arch steepens, exit right by a thin crack, turn another bulge and follow demanding face moves to a shelf where you belay. The second pitch goes leftward to a mantle over a poor landing, then climbs a corner and a steep jug-filled face to the ramp, which is the way off.
Go up the slab that faces east, clipping its two bolts.

moves.from: Walk about fifty yards west from behind Hanging Gardens, then
moves.value: Walk about fifty yards west from behind Hanging Gardens to the base of the slab.

beta_new: Start at the left end of the boulder's face and climb the face and arete, clipping two bolts, to the top.

moves.from: Get down with a single-rope rappel.

beta_new: Start below the east end of the wall at a big boulder pile. Scramble right out of the ledge full of bushes to a large crack and a clear face. Climb the east face to the knife-edged top.

moves.from: then traverse left to get down

beta_new: This route is entered from above. Cross the slab to the anchor, rappel down, and then climb back up the thin face, clipping four bolts. Expect long smearing moves rather than holds.

The first pitch climbs the face to a bolt, then continues until it clips the final bolt of Bugati Cafe's opening pitch, and ends on the little ledge where you belay. The second pitch heads almost directly up the face over the belay along four bolts spaced in a row to the summit.
Climb the face, clipping four bolts, to the stance on the shoulder over your head.

moves.from: After that you just walk off, which may feel like easy scrambling.

beta_new: Scramble easy fifth class for about twenty feet to the anchor bolts, rappel down, and then climb back up the face left of the gully, clipping four bolts to return to the anchor.
Step from the boulder onto the face, then pull a tricky unprotected move onto a solid foothold to get at a bolt. From there climb the face into a crack and follow it past a fixed piton to the top.
Share the start with the Standard Route, but where that route cuts across to the left onto easier terrain after the crux, go directly upward, clipping two bolts.
Start on the southeast face and climb the face with two bolts to a roof, then get over the roof, clipping another bolt, to reach the top.
Begin immediately right of the original start, mid-face, and climb to a bolt, then move up and left on the face to join the regular route.
Start at the left end of the wall below an overhang and climb over it, then continue up the face to a flake. At the flake's top, traverse right beyond a bolt and go up the face to finish.
